countries.notes: National: USDA NASS Crop Production 2025 Summary (Jan 2026), table "Crop Area Planted and Harvested ... United States: 2024 and 2025", ranked by 2025 harvested area (corn grain 91.3 M ac, soybeans 80.4, wheat 37.2, alfalfa hay 14.7, cotton 7.8, sorghum 6.0, rice 2.7, canola 2.3; peanuts 1.9 and barley 1.8 follow). "Hay, all other" (34.9 M ac, would rank 4th) has no clean vocabulary match (closest: grassnes/mixedgrass/fornes) and is left out of the list. States: USDA NASS 2025 State Agriculture Overview pages (survey estimates), ranked by the larger of planted/harvested acres; alfalfa = "hay & haylage, alfalfa"; non-alfalfa hay listed in unmatched. That table covers surveyed field crops, vegetables and main fruit/nuts, so minor specialty crops may be missing. Wisconsin rye is planted area (220k ac, only 14k harvested for grain: mostly cover crop). www.nass.usda.gov redirects to sb.nass.usda.gov; one transient TLS EOF on Nebraska, succeeded on retry. No US-total overview page exists (state=US returns empty), hence the separate national source.

National 2025 seeded ha: wheat 10.94 M, canola 8.76 M, tame hay 5.06 M (no clean vocabulary match; closest mixedgrass/fornes; kept in unmatched), barley 2.48 M, soybeans 2.36 M, lentils 1.77 M, grain corn 1.53 M, dry peas 1.42 M, oats 1.21 M. Potatoes are not in that table: potato area for Prince Edward Island (83,700 acres) and New Brunswick (50,900 acres) comes from StatCan table 32-10-0358-01 (https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/tbl/csv/32100358-eng.zip), latest reference year 2026, converted to hectares to place it in the ranking (potato elsewhere: Alberta 86,000 ac, Manitoba 70,500 ac, too small to enter the top 6). Gap: these tables exclude fruit, vegetables and grapes, so British Columbia (tree fruit, berries, wine grapes) and southern Ontario/Quebec horticulture are under-represented; BC marked medium for that reason.

countries.notes: SIAP (Secretaria de Agricultura) open data "Estadistica de Produccion Agricola", municipal closing file for agricultural year 2024 ("Descargar CSV" 2024 link on the page, 5.9 MB), aggregated here by state and crop over all cycles and water regimes, ranked by sown area (Sembrada, ha). National 2024 sown ha: maiz grano 6.66 M, pastos y praderas 2.58 M (sown pasture, excluded from lists, in unmatched), frijol 1.50 M, sorgo grano 1.30 M, cana 0.84 M, cafe 0.70 M, maiz forrajero 0.59 M, avena forrajera 0.55 M (no vocabulary match, closest fornes), trigo 0.49 M, naranja 0.35 M, cebada 0.30 M, aguacate 0.26 M, agave 0.24 M. "Chile seco" mapped to pimento (dry chillies), "limon" to lemonlime, "alfalfa verde"+"alfalfa achicalada" to alfalfa. 2024 was a drought year in the northwest: Sinaloa maize sown area (292k ha) is well below its usual level. Sonora (wheat) and Yucatan (mostly sown pasture) not included. Other SIAP hosts (nube.siap.gob.mx, infosiap.siap.gob.mx) did not resolve/respond; nube.agricultura.gob.mx worked.

countries.notes: National: FAOSTAT "Crops and livestock products" (QCL, https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL), Americas bulk file dated Dec 2025, element Area harvested: maize 1001k ha, coffee 376k, oil palm 230k (external-source flag), sugar cane 219k, dry beans 187k, "nutmeg, mace, cardamoms" 142k (in Guatemala this is cardamom; vocabulary key nutmeg), rubber 71k, bananas 57k. Regions: MAGA (Ministerio de Agricultura, DIPLAN) "El Agro en Cifras 2013", crop fact sheets: each sheet states which departments concentrate the harvested area of that crop, e.g. sugar cane "Escuintla (82%), Suchitepequez (11%)", cardamom "Alta Verapaz (68%), Quiche (16%)", maize "Peten (18.4%), Alta Verapaz (13.1%), Quiche (8.1%), Huehuetenango (7.5%), Jutiapa (6.6%), San Marcos (4.7%), Izabal (4%)", coffee "San Marcos (15%), Santa Rosa (14%), Huehuetenango (10%), Alta Verapaz (10%), Suchitepequez (7%), Quetzaltenango (7%)", banana "Izabal (34.3%), Escuintla (27.6%)". The per-department ORDER is a derived estimate: those department shares multiplied by FAOSTAT 2024 national harvested areas; it is not a published departmental table. Limits: only the top 2-7 departments per crop are named, so a crop is missing from a department when it falls outside that list (notably maize in Escuintla, Suchitepequez, Santa Rosa); the 2013 edition has no departmental shares for oil palm or rubber (both large nationally; oil palm is concentrated in Peten/Alta Verapaz/Izabal/south coast according to general knowledge, not verified here). FAO GIEWS country brief of 26-Jan-2026 (https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country.jsp?code=GTM) independently names Peten, Alta Verapaz and Izabal as key maize-producing departments. Not reachable: www.ine.gob.gt (bot-manager challenge, ENA survey not read), www.maga.gob.gt (403); El Agro en Cifras 2021-2023 PDFs exceed the 10 MB limit and were not downloaded.

Confidence medium only because the census is from 2011 (oil palm, coffee and groundnut areas have changed since). The census calls the two Caribbean regions RAAN and RAAS (now RACCN/RACCS). INIDE departmental profiles and the Internet Archive index were not reachable (404 / "temporarily offline").

countries.notes: National: FAOSTAT "Crops and livestock products" (QCL, https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL), Americas bulk file dated Dec 2025, element Area harvested: coffee 82.5k ha, oil palm 74.7k, sugar cane 58.3k, "other fruits n.e.c." 56.7k (FAO estimate, omitted from list; key would be fruitnes), pineapples 53.0k, bananas 45.9k, rice 14.7k, dry beans 14.7k, oranges 12.8k. Regions: NO official crop-by-province table could be read, so all seven provinces have empty crop lists. Tried: INEC VI Censo Nacional Agropecuario 2014 (inec.cr returns 403 to both curl and the fetch tool; the INAMU-hosted file https://formatos.inamu.go.cr/SIDOC/archivosLibros/tc_vi_censo_nacional_agropecuario_11417_636106476680154294.pdf is only the table of contents, which confirms that tables of area by crop "segun provincia" exist in the census volume "Cultivos agricolas, forestales y ornamentales"); SEPSA/InfoAgro series (https://www.infoagro.go.cr/estadisticas/areayproduccion_region/) are by planning region (Chorotega, Brunca, Huetar Norte...) not by province and cover only some crops; sepsa.go.cr refused connections. Uncited, last-resort hints only (Spanish Wikipedia "Agricultura en Costa Rica", not used for the lists): banana mainly in Limon; pineapple around San Carlos (Alajuela), Sarapiqui (Heredia) and Buenos Aires (Puntarenas); oil palm in the Central and South Pacific (Puntarenas). FAO GIEWS brief of 09-Jul-2026 names Chorotega and Brunca as main cropping regions without crops.

countries.notes: National: FAOSTAT "Crops and livestock products" (QCL, https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL), Americas bulk file dated Dec 2025, element Area harvested: sugar cane 270k ha (FAO estimate), cassava 124k, maize 115k (external), plantains 70k, tomatoes 43k, rice 41k, dry beans 40k, sweet potatoes 36k; all estimated/imputed, no official flags. Regions: ONEI (Oficina Nacional de Estadistica e Informacion) provincial statistical yearbooks 2023 (PDF "Archivo completo" linked from each page), chapter 7, tables "Superficie cosechada y en produccion de cultivos seleccionados de la agricultura no canera" (ha) and "Superficie cosechada ... cana de azucar por zafras" (zafra 2022/2023; 2020/2021 for Sancti Spiritus and Mayabeque, whose non-cane figures are for 2021). Harvested-area series in these yearbooks jump by up to an order of magnitude between years and some columns exclude the non-state sector, so rankings are indicative only (confidence low/medium). Fruit trees are reported only as selected items and coffee/cocoa are not in these tables. FAO GIEWS brief (https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country.jsp?code=CUB) names Granma, Sancti Spiritus, Camaguey and Pinar del Rio as the main paddy-producing areas. Access: https://www.onei.gob.cu has an EXPIRED TLS certificate (not bypassed); the site was read over its plain-HTTP address, which answers only intermittently (connection refused most of the time), so provinces with empty crop lists are those whose yearbook could not be downloaded.

What was read: MARNDR/FAO/EU Recensement General de l'Agriculture (RGA) 2008-2009, "Synthese nationale des resultats" (file HTI_REP_FRE_2008_2009.pdf in the FAO microdata catalogue, https://microdata.fao.org/index.php/catalog/1601/related-materials), Tableau 11-10: utilised agricultural area by department and by crop GROUP (cereals, legumes, vegetables incl. roots and tubers, fruits and nuts, oil crops, beverages/spices, sugar crops) in carreaux (1 cx = 1.29 ha); those group figures are recorded in "unmatched" for each department as the only sub-national evidence. FAO GIEWS brief (https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country.jsp?code=HTI) only calls Artibonite a "key producing department" without naming a crop. Not reachable: agriculture.gouv.ht (403/404).
